title: Add-on DMARDs and interstitial lung disease in methotrexate-treated rheumatoid arthritis: A prevalent new-user design study using a large regional Japanese claims database
content:
by Daito Funaki, Eiji Nakatani, Koichi Miyashita, Kentaro Minowa, Ryo Watanabe, Akinori Miyakoshi, Hideaki Kaneda, Hironao Hozumi, Akira Sugawara, Yoshihiro Tanaka

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by joint inflammation, destruction, and systemic complications including interstitial lung disease (ILD). We conducted a prevalent new-user design study using the Shizuoka Kokuho Database in Japan to examine ILD incidence after addition of non-methotrexate (MTX) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) to MTX therapy. Patients receiving sulfasalazine, tacrolimus hydrate, etanercept, iguratimod, bucillamine, or denosumab were compared with time-conditioned MTX controls using propensity score matching. Death was treated as a competing event. Among 63,952 patients with RA, 11,430 who received MTX were included in the source cohort. Gray's test indicated higher cumulative ILD incidence for sulfasalazine, tacrolimus hydrate, and bucillamine than for their matched controls (p = 0.0034, 0.0393, and 0.0477, respectively). Corresponding cause-specific hazard ratios were 1.79 (95% CI 1.21–2.66), 1.53 (1.02–2.31), and 1.75 (0.998–3.07), respectively. These findings are exploratory associations and do not establish drug-specific causality.
